blocks.text:
After did / did not / does not / Did you...? the verb stays in the base form.
He did not work. (not: did not worked)
Did you send the report? (not: Did you sent)
With need: need + to + base verb. I need to check the account.
Articles: a / an before a new singular noun, the for something already known.

s_a15_retry.label: Retry: does / did not + base verb

e01.name: Verb after did / does not
e01.note: Negatives and questions in the past got better on Nov 3. On Nov 4 'does not Worked' still appeared.
e01.right: does not work · did not go
e01.rule: After did, did not, does not and Did you...?, the verb stays in the base form. The -ed goes only on did.

e02.name: did in a positive sentence
e02.rule: In a positive past sentence, use the past verb with no did.
e02.wrong: did write · did take · did come

e03.name: he / she + -s in the present
e03.note: On Nov 4: sends and shows were right.
e03.right: He sends · He does not send
e03.rule: Positive: verb + -s. With does or does not, the verb goes back to the base form, with no -s.

e04.name: Articles a / an / the
e04.note: Also seen in 'a Claude plan' and 'the Saturday'.
e04.rule: A singular countable noun almost always needs a, an or the.

e05.name: Word class
e05.note: Your work vocabulary is already good. The problem is the form of the word.
e05.right: I build automations · supplier accounts · reconciled
e05.rule: Nouns, verbs and adjectives have different forms: analysis / analyze, account / accounting.
e05.wrong: I make automation · supply accounts · reconciliate

e06.name: need to + verb
e06.right: I need to check the supplier account
e06.rule: After need comes to + the base verb.

e07.name: Capital letters and apostrophes
e07.note: Some of this may be fast typing.
e07.rule: Days, months and names start with a capital letter. The apostrophe replaces the o in not.

e08.name: Sentence without a verb
e08.note: On Nov 4 answers are still short, but the content is right.
e08.right: Some employees were worried that the meetings would move to other days.
e08.rule: Every answer is a sentence with a subject and a verb.

e09.name: Prepositions with days and places
e09.note: Mistakes with to/for, in/on and at on Oct 31.
e09.rule: on + day (on Saturday), in + month or year (in March), at + time (at 8 pm). to and for change the meaning.

e_doesnt_base.name: Base verb after does not
e_doesnt_base.right: He does not work on Sunday.
e_doesnt_base.rule: After does / doesn't / did / didn't, the main verb stays in the base form.
e_doesnt_base.note: You did it right with "didn't go". Same rule for the present.

e_missing_verb.name: Missing main verb
e_missing_verb.right: She does not know the answer.
e_missing_verb.rule: does not is only the helper. You still need the main verb (know).
